transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

I cannot tell you which part to buy yet because 'blowing cold air' is usually caused by a safety cut-out tripping due to restricted airflow, rather than a broken component. On Beko vented dryers, the most common cause is a blocked lint filter or condenser unit. If these are clogged, the dryer overheats and cuts the heat to protect itself. Please check two things first: 1) Is the main fluff filter in the door frame full of lint? 2) Is the condenser unit (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) clean? If either is blocked, clean them thoroughly with water and let them dry completely before trying again. If they are already clean and it still blows cold air on a normal heat programme, then we can look at the heater element or thermal cut-out.

Lint filter was fairly full, I've cleaned it now. It's a vented one with a hose out the window, so no condenser. The hose had a sag full of fluff which I've cleared too, but it's still cold after 20 mins. Dryer says DV7110 on the front. Which part is it?

I cannot give you the exact part number yet because I haven't confirmed which component has failed, but on your Beko DV7110 vented dryer, if the airflow is clear and it still blows cold air after 20 minutes, the most likely cause is a failed heater element. The thermal cut-out (a safety device) may also have tripped or failed as a result of previous overheating. To be sure, you need to check for continuity on the heater element using a multimeter. This involves isolating the dryer (unplugging it), removing the back panel or top panel (depending on your specific model's construction) to access the heating assembly, and testing the resistance across the element terminals. If there is no continuity (infinite resistance), the element has failed open and needs replacing. Are you comfortable performing this multimeter check? If so, I can guide you through the safe steps to locate and test it.
No, I haven't got a multimeter so I can't do that test. Is there any way to tell which part it is without one, or should I just order the element and the thermal cut-out?

You cannot reliably tell which part has failed without a multimeter because both the heater element and the thermal cut-out can cause 'cold air' symptoms. However, on your Beko DV7110, if you have already cleaned the filter and cleared the vent hose, it is likely that the heater element has failed open (stopped working). The thermal cut-out may also be blown as a result of previous overheating. Since you cannot test them electrically, the standard repair approach for this specific symptom on a vented dryer with clear airflow is to check both the heater element and the thermal cut-out together. I recommend ordering these two parts; if only one fails, replacing both ensures the fault is fully resolved.

candidates: Blocked airflow (filter/condenser) tripping the thermal cut-out (high)
Failed heater element or thermal cut-out (medium)
